claims.text: HfNbTaTiZr is an equiatomic alloy system.
The initial equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr is in the cast state.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Untreated HfNbTaTiZr has inadequate oxygen resistance for high-temperature use in air.
An anti-oxidation coating can improve the suitability of HfNbTaTiZr for high-temperature use in air.
A few-micrometre Al2O3 coating can be deposited on cast HfNbTaTiZr by atomic layer deposition.
The alumina coating will remain protective during exposure to air at approximately 1000 °C for 100 hours.
The applied alumina will form a continuous, dense protective layer.
The continuous, dense alumina layer will act as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
The alumina coating will prevent direct oxygen contact with the underlying alloy.
Restricting oxygen contact will reduce oxidation-induced embrittlement.
The coating process and subsequent exposure will leave the alloy's bulk microstructure essentially unmodified.
Coated samples will show less oxidation weight gain and a thinner oxidation layer than untreated samples.
The coating will preserve approximately the same high-temperature yield strength as untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The coating will preserve approximately the same room-temperature tensile ductility as untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The coating's long-term adhesion and durability under cyclic thermal and mechanical loading are uncertain.
Coating-induced surface stresses may affect mechanical performance.

contradictions.description: The conditions and boundary imply that the 100-hour oxidation exposure occurs under mechanical loading at stated strain rates, whereas the experiment describes an unloaded exposure followed by separate tensile tests.
